stem: A nurse develops an unusually strong emotional response to a client that is shaped by the nurse's own past experiences and relationships. What is this phenomenon?

options.A: Transference, in which the client redirects feelings from past relationships toward the nurse.
options.B: Regression, in which stress is associated with a return to earlier patterns of coping or behavior.
options.C: Projection, in which a person attributes personal feelings, impulses, or characteristics to another person.
options.D: Countertransference, in which the nurse's own feelings or past experiences shape reactions toward the client.

rationale: Countertransference occurs when the clinician transfers personal feelings into the current therapeutic relationship and those reactions may influence the client. D therefore matches the stem. A describes transference from the client toward the nurse. B describes regression to an earlier level of functioning under stress. C describes attributing one's own characteristics, feelings, or impulses to another person.
educational_objective: Distinguish countertransference, which originates in the clinician's own reactions, from client transference and common defense mechanisms such as regression and projection.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
source_document_title: Nursing: Mental Health and Community Concepts, 2nd edition — Chapter 4 Application of the Nursing Process to Mental Health Care; Table 3.4 Common Defense Mechanisms
source_locator: Chapter 4 > Mental Status Examination > Attitude and Insight (transference) and Examiner's Reaction to the Client (countertransference); Table 3.4 Common Defense Mechanisms > Projection and Regression rows
source_claim_supported: The current Open RN 2nd edition defines transference as client-to-nurse transfer of feelings and countertransference as examiner-to-client transfer of the examiner's own feelings; its defense-mechanism table separately defines regression and projection.
